Each button's top legs (side 1) go to the signal strip with the wire from the Arduino pin; its bottom legs (side 2) go to the strip with a black wire to the bottom negative (ground) rail. Pins use INPUT_PULLUP so no resistors are needed.

Pot: red wire from the positive rail (fed from the Arduino IOREF pin) to the VCC end, yellow wire from A0 to the wiper (SIG), black wire from the bottom negative rail to the GND end. The slide pot is modelled as potentiometer-10k.
Arduino GND pin used is the one on the digital header next to AREF; modelled as GND.1 (catalogue port naming ambiguity).

The two black rail-to-rail wires (Arduino GND to top negative rail, and top negative rail to bottom negative rail) link all ground rails; the top and bottom negative rails are not otherwise connected.
The 7 tactile buttons were listed as 'None' in the matched parts but the catalogue's pushbutton type is used.

notes: The catalogue auto-match 'Diode -> led' is wrong; a new `diode` type (A anode, C cathode) is used. '0.1 uF ceramic capacitor -> capacitor-22pf' is also wrong; `capacitor-100nf` is used.
The Arduino MKR Zero is in the catalogue, so `arduino-mkr-zero` is used. The microphone, diode and rubber band are new part types.

The schematic image was not available, so the breadboard layout, hole positions and rail assignments are my own, built from the text and the parts photo. Rails: tp = 3.3V (MKR VCC), tn = GND, bp = 5V, bn = GND. The two GND rails are joined by a wire.
The manual gives only the I2S pins (SD on A6, SCK on 2, FS/WS on 3). The motor MOSFET gate pin (6) and servo PWM pin (5) are assumed.

The DC motor is switched low-side by MOSFET q1. Its 2.2k pull-down r1 sits on the gate, and the flyback diode d1 runs from drain (anode) to the 5V side (cathode). The 0.1 uF capacitor c1 is placed across the motor terminals, as in the photo of the motor.

The servo signal goes through MOSFET q2 as a 3.3V-to-5V level shifter: gate to 3.3V, source to the MKR pin, drain to the servo PWM with a 2.2k pull-up r2 to 5V. The 100 uF electrolytic capacitor c2 sits across the 5V and GND rails next to the servo.
Microphone power is 3.3V (ICS43432 VDD) and its L/R pin is tied to GND. The microphone is a 6-pin breakout in the top half of the breadboard.
The servo and DC motor leads are modelled as plugged directly into breadboard holes. In reality, jumper or soldered leads are used.

The MDF laser-cut box, wheel, lifting arm and hot glue are not electrical parts and are omitted. The rubber band is included with a contact edge to the DC motor (it is woven onto the wheel on the motor gear).
The photo shows 'MKRZERO' printed on the bills (a stack of paper), not a part.
